Methods for FCA indices on numeric data

Source: R/08-spax_access_values.R
spax_access_values-methods.Rd

What to do with the result of spax() for an FCA specification (spec_e2sfca() and the others) on numeric data (prep_data() with demand, supply and a travel matrix): a list with access, a matrix with one row per active origin (named by the origin IDs) and one column per layer, type, parameters, facilities and call. With demand groups the columns are supply.<group> and supply.all, the layers of the raster route. Origins that are not in the data (zero demand, unknown demand, left out) have no row and so no value.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'spax_access_values'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_access_values'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_access_values'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.spax_access_values'
print(x, digits = 4L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_access_values'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x, object

A spax_access_values, or for print() of the summary, a summary.spax_access_values.

...

Unused.

digits

Number of significant digits printed in the summary.

row.names, optional

Standard as.data.frame() arguments.

Value

print() returns its argument invisibly, summary() a summary.spax_access_values and as.data.frame() a data frame.

Details

  • print() shows the type, the layers, the decay and the normalization.

  • summary() returns a summary.spax_access_values: for each layer the number of origins with a value, its minimum, mean and maximum, and the coverage, the origins whose access is above zero and their proportion.

  • as.data.frame() gives the table of the access values: origin_id and one column per layer.

See also

spax(), prep_data()

Other allocation interface: decay_gaussian(), obs_flows(), prep_data(), spax(), spax_allocation-methods, spax_huff(), spec_clm()

Examples

# Mainland Cornwall: residents by small area, GP FTE by practice and the
# travel minutes between them
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa[!cornwall_lsoa$scilly, ])
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp[!cornwall_gp$scilly, ])
d <- prep_data(stats::setNames(areas$pop, areas$lsoa),
               stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice),
               cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice])

# E2SFCA with a Gaussian decay of 10 minutes, at the small areas
access <- spax(d, spec_e2sfca(decay_gaussian(sigma = 10)))
access
#> <spax access> E2SFCA, 1 layer at 336 origins x 54 facilities
#>   layers      supply
#>   decay       gaussian (sigma = 10)
#>   normalize   identity
summary(access)
#> <spax access summary> E2SFCA
#>   origins     336
#>   decay       gaussian (sigma = 10)
#>   normalize   identity
#> 
#>   layer with_value       min      mean       max covered proportion
#>  supply        336 0.0001679 0.0005318 0.0007182     336          1
head(as.data.frame(access))
#>   origin_id       supply
#> 1 E01018750 0.0005968168
#> 2 E01018751 0.0005968168
#> 3 E01018752 0.0006006746
#> 4 E01018753 0.0003819479
#> 5 E01018754 0.0003194073
#> 6 E01018755 0.0002856953
